name: Stripe
h1_tail: Funding Rounds, Share Prices and Ownership
description: Stripe is privately held and has no ticker. Review the price of each funding round, the investors, funds and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Stripe is a privately held financial technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the prices at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a Series I round of more than $6.5 billion announced on March 15, 2023, valued the company at $50 billion. A tender offer for employee shares that Stripe announced on February 24, 2026 valued the company at $159 billion.

Founded in 2010 and based in South San Francisco, California, Stripe provides payment processing and related financial software to businesses that sell online and in person. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.

table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. Tender offers for existing shares are not shown.
round_notes: Stripe has said the Series I proceeds were used to provide liquidity to current and former employees and to pay withholding taxes on employee equity awards. The February 2026 tender offer was funded mainly by Thrive Capital, Coatue and Andreessen Horowitz, with Stripe also repurchasing shares; an earlier tender offer, announced in February 2025, valued the company at $91.5 billion. In September 2025, Bloomberg reported that Stripe's valuation had risen to $106.7 billion; Stripe did not comment on the report.

A round price reflects what investors paid for the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: The Series I brought in GIC, Temasek and Goldman Sachs as new investors, alongside existing backers including Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst and Founders Fund. Sequoia Capital, Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Axa and Allianz X invested in the Series H, as did Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency. Other investors include GV, MSD Partners and Coatue.
spv_sentence: Since 2021, 23 special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Stripe have filed with the SEC, nine of them in 2026.
funds: Mutual funds and other SEC-registered funds managed by Capital Group, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock and Fundrise, among others, reported Stripe holdings in filings for periods in 2026. Capital Group's Growth Fund of America valued its position at $770.1 million as of May 31, 2026. As of July 31, 2026, ARK Venture Fund held 754,148 shares, which it valued at $53.4 million, or $70.82 per share.
sources: Sources: Stripe's announcements of its Series I and Series H and of its tender offers in February 2026 and February 2025; reports by TechCrunch (February 2026 and April 2020), CNBC (March 2023) and Bloomberg (September 2025); ARK Venture Fund's Form N-PORT for July 31, 2026; and SEC Form D and Form N-PORT filings.
